findings.text: Only 164 of the 403 readmes have Haiku's `shape` and `note`; the other 239 are blank in the Shape column (audit.jsonl latest lines: 157 mixed, 5 index, 2 essay, 239 none, $5.99). This is the $6 cap working as briefed and it is stated in readme-system.md:46, but the full Haiku run (about $14 more) is still open and should be filed as a task, not left in the log line.

`ReadmeAudit.readmes()` (Server/ReadmeAudit.mjs:37-48) copies the walk in `ReadmeChains.rows()` (Server/ReadmeChains.mjs:16-33) line for line and shares only `SKIP`. Exporting one `ReadmeChains.dirs()` walk for both would stop the two lists from drifting apart (law 6). Today both find 403.

The `unnamed` check is a case-insensitive substring match (Server/ReadmeAudit.mjs:55), so a short name hides inside a longer word: a file `page` or `Task.js` counts as named whenever the readme says "pages" or "SubTask.js". This gives false negatives only, which is fine for pass 1; pass 2 should match whole names before it trusts the field.

The committed shot is `readmes-1920.png`, taken before commit d0eaa1494 fixed the clipped Shape column. The corrected `readmes-1920-after.png` sits untracked in the task folder, so the record in git shows the bug. Commit the after shot.

Folders deep in the tree can't be told apart without clicking them.

Dead links still include some false positives from virtual routes (the session log says so). `site_route` (Server/ReadmeAudit.mjs:60-65) covers `/Servex`, `/framework/servex` and `/md/`, so read the 118 readmes with dead links as an upper bound.
